unmutated.M1:constant-mosaic: The zero-input corner of M1:totality-agrees-with-evaluator: one part, no inputs, so the one empty tuple must draw that part. NoOpMosaic fails it, but the entry targets totality, and the display and panel loops in totality already compare the plan to the oracle on every state of every input. The manifest half of the same corner is M4:constant-manifest. Only a plan that special-cases a mosaic with no inputs can break it, and no pluggable step of the compiler has a reason to.
unmutated.M1:empty-mosaic-draws-nothing: A positive control on the zero-part corner: a mosaic with no parts and no inputs must assemble to nothing. NoOpMosaic satisfies it by construction, and no fixture in the matrix draws something from nothing. Breaking it needs a plan that fabricates a part for an empty picture, such as a default core, which M1:totality-agrees-with-evaluator would reject on any non-empty mosaic that did the same. It guards the harness against an oracle that cannot say 'nothing', not an implementation.
unmutated.M1:guard-and-template-together: A hand-written expectation of M1:totality-agrees-with-evaluator for one state: the part that has both a guard and a template (display_glow_{north}) expands to display_glow_sun at index 6. The exhaustive totality check compares the plan to the oracle on all 512 states, including that one, so it covers the same ground; SwappedOrder and NoOpMosaic also fail this label incidentally. It exists to prove the oracle and the plan do not share a mistake about templates.
unmutated.M1:guard-over-a-subset-of-values: A hand-written expectation of M1:totality-agrees-with-evaluator for one state: a guard listing moon and sun excludes star, so six parts, not seven. NoOpMosaic fails it incidentally. It is a check on the scenario and the oracle, not on an implementation.
unmutated.M1:hand-checked-dark-state: A check on the oracle itself, not on an implementation: the expected picture for one dark state is written out by hand, so the independent oracle used by M1:totality-agrees-with-evaluator cannot be wrong in step with the plan. Any plan that differs from the oracle on this state also fails totality, which is the targeted label (NoOpMosaic); ReversedTurn, SwappedOrder and NoOpMosaic fail this one incidentally.
unmutated.M1:hand-checked-lit-state: A check on the oracle itself, not on an implementation: the expected picture for one lit state, with all seven parts and two templates, is written out by hand, so the independent oracle behind M1:totality-agrees-with-evaluator cannot be wrong in step with the plan. Any plan that differs from the oracle on this state also fails totality, which is the targeted label (NoOpMosaic); ReversedTurn, SwappedOrder and NoOpMosaic fail this one incidentally.

unmutated.M1:properties-hold-on-random-mosaics: An aggregate, not a law of its own: it is the conjunction of M1 (agreement with the oracle), M4 (exact manifest), M6 (canonical bytes) and the resource read-back over 40 seeded random mosaics, each of which has its own label. It is failed by six of the eight entries (ReversedTurn, SwappedOrder, ManifestOmitsTemplates, ManifestOverreach, HashOrderEmitter, NoOpMosaic) because it repeats their targets on other shapes, so a target on it would add nothing; it exists to catch a compiler that is right only on the hand-built display and panel.
unmutated.M1:unread-input-dropped: Not held by any entry: the plan's mosaic is Mosaic.pruned(), applied inside ReferenceMosaic.compile, and no matrix fixture replaces the step that hands the plan its mosaic. This allowance is a gap, not a reason: a compiler that does not prune is cheap and realistic.

No block fixture makes a plan trust a value of the wrong kind; it is the same newPlan-level mutant as for the other two default readings.
unmutated.M2:swapped-parts-draw-swapped: The end-to-end twin of M6:part-order-is-kept: the same display with its first two parts exchanged must draw the exchanged order. The compile-time half, a compiler that sorts parts into a canonical order, is not held by any entry and is a mutant worth writing: it would fail this label and M6:part-order-is-kept.

With the input dropped there is nothing left to vary; even kept, glow values 0 and 3 are both in domain, so Assembly equality would still hold for the reference assembler. No realistic mistake in the compiler's pluggable steps produces a plan that reads a field nothing asks for.
unmutated.M4:constant-manifest: The zero-input corner of M4:manifest-covers-every-drawn-model: a mosaic with one unconditional part lists exactly that model. unmutated.M4:empty-manifest: The zero-part corner of M4:manifest-has-no-undrawn-model (ManifestOverreach): a mosaic with no parts lists no model. Breaking it needs a manifest that always names a fallback or missing-model entry, which the extra-model direction already rejects on every non-empty mosaic; it guards the harness against an oracle that cannot say 'empty'.

unmutated.M6:part-order-is-kept: Not held by any entry: it asserts that exchanging two parts changes the artefacts, so the order of parts is not normalised away. It would also fail M2:swapped-parts-draw-swapped and totality, so it is a good mutant to write.
unmutated.M6:repeat-identical: Not held by any entry: HashOrderEmitter is deterministic within a run (a HashMap iterates the same way twice), so it passes.
